claim_verdicts.evidence: "The direction of dependency within the application should be in the direction of abstraction, not implementation details." (:35) and "implementation details can be written to depend on and implement higher-level abstractions, rather than the other way around" (:47); inversion = "for B to depend on an interface controlled by A at compile time (thus, inverting the typical compile-time dependency)" (:41). Supports section 3 definition and section 4 'both sides depend on the abstraction'.

git show stage-0:.../PlaceOrderSplit.cs lines 36-37: "private static void Notify(int customerId) => Console.WriteLine($\"sending an email to customer {customerId}\");". The string INotifier does not occur anywhere in the file (git grep INotifier stage-0 hits only INotifier.cs:5 and NotifierBase.cs:5).

git grep -n INotifier stage-0 (whole repo, incl. samples/DonHang.Samples.Tests) returns exactly two hits: Oop/INotifier.cs:5 'public interface INotifier' and Oop/NotifierBase.cs:5 'public abstract class NotifierBase : INotifier'.

INotifier.cs:7 'void Send(int orderId, string subject);'. NotifierBase.cs:5 'public abstract class NotifierBase : INotifier', :21 'public sealed class EmailNotifier : NotifierBase' overriding Format -> "email about order {orderId}: {subject}", :27 'public sealed class SmsNotifier : NotifierBase' -> "sms about order {orderId}: {subject}".

"Three situations always produce an implicit reference conversion: assigning a derived class instance to a base class variable ..., assigning a reference type instance to a variable of an interface the type implements, and assigning any reference type to an object variable." EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier implement INotifier through NotifierBase, so both conversions apply.

ASP.NET Core DI docs, on a class that does 'new MyDependency()' itself: "To replace MyDependency with a different implementation, the consuming class must be modified." Architecture guide: developers "tightly couple their code to specific implementations through direct instantiation. 'New is glue' is meant to be a reminder of this coupling". Variable type does not change this.

"The practice of dependency injection is made possible by following the dependency inversion principle." (architectural-principles.md:47); "Dependency injection is a technique ... Dependency injection is based on the dependency inversion principle" (develop-asp-net-core-mvc-apps.md:180). Principle and mechanism are presented as distinct.

NotifierBase.cs:23-24 @ stage-0: EmailNotifier.Format returns $"email about order {orderId}: {subject}"; :11-13 Send(int orderId, string subject) passes the caller's subject into Format. Fixed part lives in Format, subject comes from the caller of Send. Matches the new Try-it item 3 and its expected result.

"The class must provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface" (:35); but "Default interface members let an interface provide a method body. Implementing types inherit the default implementation" (:78) and "must provide implementations for all declared members (unless the interface provides a default implementation)" (:86). So 'any change requires changing the implementer' misses that condition. Here the implementer is NotifierBase; EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier implement INotifier only through it.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A class implementing an interface must provide an implementation for every member the interface declares, so changing a declared member such as Send's parameters forces a change in the implementing class (here NotifierBase, through which EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier implement INotifier).

issues.text: Overstated: C# requires an implementation for every declared member (unless the interface gives a default body), not an exact match to 'what it declares'; and the implementing class is NotifierBase, not EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier directly (Send is in NotifierBase). A change to INotifier reaches the concrete classes through NotifierBase. See claim 9.
issues.quote: implementing it means they must match exactly what it declares, so a change to it reaches them.
issues.fix: Replace with: "implementing it means providing every method it declares, so if `Send` changed, `NotifierBase` — and with it `EmailNotifier` and `SmsNotifier` — would have to change too." Update claim 9 to the suggested_text.
